# `uring` standard library

The `uring` module provides low-level Linux `io_uring` kernel submission and completion rings
for non-blocking asynchronous system calls.

```{.dva .run}
#use uring
```

## Platform requirements

The `uring` module depends directly on the Linux kernel `io_uring` interface (kernel 5.1+).
It is available exclusively on Linux targets.

> [!NOTE]
> Even on supported kernels, environment policies (such as restrictive Docker seccomp profiles,
> unprivileged container namespaces, or system-wide `kernel.io_uring_disabled` sysctl settings)
> can cause `uring::new` to fail with runtime permission or operation errors.

## Core structures

```{.dva .partial}
#type CQE (
   user_data: Int,
   res:       Int,
   flags:     Int
)

#type Ring (
   fd:          Int,
   sq_ptr:      Addr,
   sq_sz:       Int,
   sqes_ptr:    Addr,
   sqes_sz:     Int,
   cq_ptr:      Addr,
   cq_sz:       Int,
   sq_head_off: Int,
   sq_tail_off: Int,
   sq_mask_off: Int,
   sq_arr_off:  Int,
   cq_head_off: Int,
   cq_tail_off: Int,
   cq_mask_off: Int,
   cq_cqes_off: Int,
   sq_entries:  Int,
   cq_entries:  Int
)
```

## Function catalog

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `uring::new` | `Int => < Ring \| String >` | Initializes an `io_uring` ring with the requested number of submission queue entries |
| `uring::prep_nop` | `Ring, Int => <>` | Prepares a no-operation submission; returns `<->` if the queue is full |
| `uring::prep_read` | `Ring, Int, Addr, Int, Int => <>` | Prepares an asynchronous read at current file offset (`-1`), advancing position on completion |
| `uring::prep_read_at` | `Ring, Int, Addr, Int, Int, Int => <>` | Prepares an asynchronous read at an explicit file offset (`off`), preserving file position |
| `uring::prep_write` | `Ring, Int, Addr, Int, Int => <>` | Prepares an asynchronous write at current file offset (`-1`), advancing position on completion |
| `uring::prep_write_at` | `Ring, Int, Addr, Int, Int, Int => <>` | Prepares an asynchronous write at an explicit file offset (`off`), preserving file position |
| `uring::prep_close` | `Ring, Int, Int => <>` | Prepares an asynchronous file descriptor close operation |
| `uring::prep_send` | `Ring, Int, Addr, Int, Int, Int => <>` | Prepares an asynchronous socket send operation |
| `uring::prep_recv` | `Ring, Int, Addr, Int, Int, Int => <>` | Prepares an asynchronous socket receive operation |
| `uring::prep_accept` | `Ring, Int, Addr, Addr, Int, Int => <>` | Prepares an asynchronous socket accept operation |
| `uring::prep_timeout` | `Ring, Addr, Int, Int, Int => <>` | Prepares a timer- or completion-count-based timeout |
| `uring::prep_cancel` | `Ring, Int, Int => <>` | Prepares an asynchronous cancellation request targeting a 64-bit `user_data` |
| `uring::sq_space` | `Ring => Int` | Returns the number of available slots remaining in the submission queue |
| `uring::submit` | `Ring => Int` | Enters kernel and submits pending SQEs via `io_uring_enter` |
| `uring::submit_and_wait` | `Ring, Int => Int` | Submits pending SQEs and blocks until at least `wait_nr` CQEs complete |
| `uring::peek_cqe` | `Ring => < CQE \| >` | Non-blocking check for a completion event; copies CQE before advancing head pointer |
| `uring::wait_cqe` | `Ring => < CQE \| String >` | Checks for ready CQE or blocks via `submit_and_wait(ring, 1)` |
| `uring::reap` | `Ring => CQEs` | Drains all currently ready CQEs into a growable array |
| `uring::close` | `Ring => ()` | Unmaps submission/completion ring memory and closes the ring file descriptor |

## Operational semantics

### Submission queue capacity

Submission queue preparation (`prep_*`) checks available ring capacity (`sq_space(ring)`).
If the ring is full, preparation returns `<->` immediately without modifying `sq_tail` or
overwriting pending submissions. Callers must invoke `uring::submit` to flush pending
entries and free ring capacity.

### Buffer lifetimes and memory stability

Standard operations (`prep_read`, `prep_write`, `prep_send`, `prep_recv`) use ordinary
buffered/page-cache I/O rather than zero-copy memory registrations. The memory buffers passed
as `Addr` are borrowed by the kernel for the duration of the asynchronous operation.
User code must ensure buffers remain valid, unmoved, and unfreed until the corresponding
completion event (`CQE`) has been reaped.

`uring::close(ring)` immediately unmaps the ring buffers and closes the kernel file descriptor.
Rings must not be closed while operations referencing user buffers remain outstanding.

### Completion queue results

Completed operations report kernel status in `CQE.res`:
- **Success**: Non-negative value (`res >= 0`), such as the number of bytes transferred.
- **Error**: Negative value (`res < 0`), matching the negative Linux errno (for example, `-62` for `-ETIME` on timeout expiration, or `-125` for `-ECANCELED`).

## Example

```{.dva .complete}
#use io
#use uring

ring_res = uring::new(8)
ring_res
   | ring =>
      uring::prep_nop(ring, 100)
      uring::submit(ring)
      cqe_opt = uring::wait_cqe(ring)
      cqe_opt
         | cqe => io::out(cqe.user_data)
      uring::close(ring)
```
